slides.title: A strategy nobody consults is [not strategy].
slides.lede: A useful brand strategy document records the choices that decide how you compete, and changes decisions where they are made.

slides.title: "Trusted and high quality" is an [input], not a decision
slides.text: Most competitors can say exactly the same thing. A decision becomes strategic when it forces a trade-off, such as competing on specialist certainty, not lowest cost.

cards.label: Strategy
cards.text: Answers why this choice: audience, positioning, value, messages.

cards.label: Guidelines
cards.text: Answers how to apply it: logo, colour, typography, tone.

slides.title: Six sections a useful document [should contain]

items.title: Commercial context
items.text: What the business must achieve next.

items.title: Priority audiences
items.text: Triggers, concerns, alternatives and proof they need.

items.title: Positioning
items.text: Audience, category, primary value, reason to believe.

items.title: Message hierarchy
items.text: One principal message, with supporting proof beneath.

items.title: Personality and voice
items.text: Stable character, tone adapted to context.

items.title: Governance
items.text: Owner, approvers, change log, review triggers.

slides.title: Review by [trigger], not calendar alone
slides.note: Not every trigger needs a rewrite. **Record what changed and who approved it.**

slides.quote: If it could describe every competitor, it is too broad.
slides.text: Write the positioning statement, then check whether it excludes something.

slides.title: Make difficult choices easier and inconsistent behaviour harder.
slides.lede: What a brand strategy document actually contains. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
